Surah Al-Mu'minun (The Believers) [Meccan; its verses are 118 or 119; it was revealed after Al-Anbiya']

﴿Qad﴾ (indeed; a particle of confirmation) ﴿aflaha﴾ (succeeded, won through)
Those who are humbly submissive in their prayer (الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلاتهمْ خاشِعُونَ), meaning humble (مُتَواضِعُونَ).
﴿And those who turn away from vain talk﴾: from idle speech and other things.
﴿And those who are active in giving zakat﴾ paying it.
﴿And those who guard their private parts﴾ from what is unlawful.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 6:

﴿Except from their spouses﴾, i.e., from their wives, ﴿or what their right hands possess﴾, i.e., the captive women (sarari), ﴿for indeed they are not blameworthy﴾ in having intercourse with them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 23, verse 7:

﴿Whoever seeks beyond that﴾ — beyond the wives and the concubines — such as masturbation by hand, in lieu of relations with them, ﴿those are the transgressors﴾, those who exceed to what is not lawful for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 8:

﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts﴾ (plural and singular), ﴿and their covenant﴾ among themselves, or among themselves and Allah, such as the prayer and other things, ﴿are keepers﴾, guardians.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 9:

﴿And those who are over their prayers﴾ — "prayers" (ṣalawāt) read both as a plural and as a singular — ﴿they guard﴾ — they establish them at their appointed times.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 10:

﴿Those are the inheritors﴾, not others.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 11:

﴿Those who inherit the Firdaws (Paradise); they will abide therein eternally.﴾ It is the garden, the highest of the gardens. ﴿They will abide therein eternally.﴾ In that is an allusion to the Return (al-ma'ad), and the mention of the Origin (al-mabda') after it is fitting to it.

﴿And﴾ Allah ﴿certainly created the human being﴾, Adam, ﴿from an extract﴾ (*sulālah*). Here ﴿sulālah﴾ is from "سَلَلْتُ الشَّيْءَ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ", meaning "I extracted the thing from the thing," and it is its essence (خُلاصَته) ﴿from clay﴾. ﴿From clay﴾ is grammatically dependent on (مُتَعَلِّق بِ) ﴿sulālah﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 13:

﴿Then We made him﴾ i.e., man, the offspring of Adam, ﴿a drop (nutfah) of semen﴾ (maniyy), ﴿in a secure place﴾, which is the womb (rahm).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 14:

﴿Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot﴾, [i.e., congealed] blood, ﴿then We made the clot into a lump of flesh﴾, [i.e., a piece of flesh] of the amount that can be chewed, ﴿then We made the lump into bones, and clothed the bones with flesh﴾. In another reading, it is "bone" (ʿaẓman) in both places. And "We made" (khalaqnā) in the three places is in the sense of "We turned into" (ṣayyarnā). ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, by breathing the spirit into it. ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾, i.e., the best of those who determine [or fashion]. The comparative "best" (aḥsan) has an omitted specifier (mumayyiz) known from context, i.e., "creation" (khalqan).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 16:

﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, you will be raised up﴾ for the reckoning and the recompense.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 17:

﴿And We have certainly created above you seven paths﴾, i.e., heavens; ṭarā'iq is the plural of ṭarīqah, because they are the paths of the angels. ﴿And We have never been, of the creation﴾ that is beneath them, ﴿unaware﴾ that they might fall upon them and destroy them. Rather, We hold them up, as a sign, ﴿and We hold back the sky from falling upon the earth﴾.

And We sent down water from the sky in measure, [in an amount] sufficient for them, ﴿and We caused it to settle in the earth, and indeed We are able to take it away.﴾ [If We did so] they would die of thirst along with their animals.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 19:

﴿Then We produced for you therewith gardens of palm trees and grapes.﴾ They are the most abundant fruits of the Arabs. ﴿For you therein are many fruits, and from them you eat.﴾ In summer and in winter.

Translation:

And We brought forth a tree growing out of Mount Sinai (ṭūr Saynāʾ), a mountain, pronounced with both a kasra and a fatḥa on the sīn, and it is treated as non-diptote (not taking nunation) because it is a proper name (ʿalamiyya) and feminine because it denotes a place (buqʿa), [which] grows with oil (bi-l-duhn), the bāʾ being extra (zāʾida) according to the first reading, and making transitive (muʿaddiya) according to the second; and it is the olive tree, and a condiment (ṣibgh) for those who eat, coordinated (ʿaṭf) with "oil", meaning a relish in which one dips the morsel and so colours it, and it is olive oil.

﴿And indeed for you in the cattle﴾ the camels, cows and sheep ﴿is a lesson﴾, an admonition by which you take heed. ﴿We give you to drink﴾ (نُسْقِيكُمْ), read with the nun vowelled with a fatha (نَسْقِيكُمْ) and with a damma (نُسْقِيكُمْ), ﴿from what is in their bellies﴾, namely the milk. ﴿And for you therein are many benefits﴾, from the wool, the fur and the hair, and other things besides that.
﴿And upon them﴾ the camels, ﴿and upon the ships﴾ the boats.

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship Allah"﴾ obey Allah and affirm His oneness. ﴿"You have no god other than Him"﴾ It is the ism (اسم, grammatical noun) of mā, and what precedes it, lakum, is the khabar (خبر, predicate), and min is zā'ida (زائدة, extra). ﴿"Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ fear His punishment through your worship of other than Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 24:

﴿So the chiefs of those who disbelieved among his people said﴾ to their followers, ﴿"This is none but a human being like you, who wants to make himself superior (yatafaddal, to elevate himself in rank) over you"﴾ by being the one who is followed while you are his followers. ﴿"And if God had willed"﴾ that He not be worshipped other than Him, ﴿"He would have sent down angels"﴾ with this message, not a human being. ﴿"We never heard of this"﴾ which Noah called to, of monotheism, ﴿"among our forefathers of old"﴾, that is, the past nations.
﴿He is not﴾ [meaning: Nuh is not] ﴿but a man in whom there is madness﴾ [meaning: a state of insanity], ﴿so wait for him﴾ [meaning: await him] ﴿for a time﴾ [meaning: until the time of his death].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 26:

﴿He said﴾ Nuh [said], ﴿"My Lord, support me"﴾ against them ﴿because they have denied me﴾, by reason of their denying me, by [causing] You to destroy them. ﴿He said﴾ — Exalted is He — answering his supplication.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 27:

﴿So We revealed to him: Build the ship﴾ (al-Fulk), the vessel, ﴿under Our eyes﴾, in plain view of Us and under Our protection, ﴿and Our inspiration﴾, that is, Our command. ﴿Then when Our command comes﴾ to destroy them, ﴿and the oven boils over﴾ (al-Tannur), the baker's oven, with water, and this was a sign for Nuh. ﴿Then load into it﴾, that is, enter into the ship, ﴿from every pair, two﴾, a male and a female, that is, from every kind of them, ﴿two﴾, a male and a female. This is the object (maf'ul), and "from" (min) is attached to "load" (usluk). It is related in the story that Allah the Exalted gathered for Nuh the beasts, the birds and others, and he began striking with his hands at each kind, so that his right hand fell on the male and his left on the female, and he would carry them in the ship. In another reading, "kullu" is read with tanwin, so that "zawjayn" is the object and "ithnayn" is an emphasis of it. ﴿And your family﴾, his wife and his children, ﴿except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ from among them, for destruction, and they are his wife and his son Kan'an, unlike Sam, Ham and Yafith. So he carried them and their wives, three (sons and their wives). And in Surat Hud: ﴿And those who believed, and only a few believed with him﴾. It has been said they were six men and their wives; and it has been said that all who were in the ship were seventy-eight, half of them men and half of them women. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong﴾, that is, those who disbelieved, by not sparing them from destruction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 28:

﴿Then when you and those with you are settled [istawayta] upon the ship﴾, [meaning] you have become upright and balanced, ﴿then say: "Praise be to Allah, who has delivered us from the wrongdoing people"﴾, [meaning] the disbelievers, and [Allah's] destruction of them.

﴿And say﴾ upon your alighting from the ship, ﴿"My Lord, cause me to alight [at a place]"﴾ — *munzalan*, with a *ḍamma* on the *mīm* and a *fatḥa* on the *zāy*, is a *maṣdar* (verbal noun) and also an *ism makān* (noun of place); with a *fatḥa* on the *mīm* and a *kasra* on the *zāy*, it means the place of alighting — ﴿blessed﴾ (*mubārakan*), meaning that alighting or that place, ﴿and You are the best of those who cause to alight﴾ of what has been mentioned.

Verse 30: "Indeed in that" (referring to what was mentioned of the matter of Noah, the ship, and the destruction of the disbelievers) "are signs" (proofs) "of the power of Allah, the Exalted. And indeed" (the "in" here is a lightened form of the heavy "inna," and its noun is the pronoun of the matter/situation) "We were ever testing" (examining) "the people of Noah by sending him to them and admonishing them."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 31:

﴿Then We brought into being after them a generation﴾ (meaning) a people ﴿other﴾ (than them), ﴿they were the ʿĀd﴾
Then We sent among them a messenger from themselves, [namely] Hud, [saying] "that" (bi-an) "worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then fear [His punishment] and believe?"

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 33:

﴿And the chiefs of his people, those who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter﴾ — by arriving at it — ﴿and whom We had made affluent in the life of this world﴾ — We had given them comfort (naʿʿamnāhum).

﴿And﴾ by Allah, ﴿if you obey a human being like yourselves﴾. In it there is an oath (qasam) and a condition (shart). The response (jawab) belongs to the first of the two, and it suffices without a separate response for the second. ﴿Indeed you would then be losers﴾, i.e., if you obeyed him, you would be defrauded (maghbunun).

**Quranic verse:** ﴿Does he promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?﴾

**Grammatical note:** The clause ﴿أنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ﴾ (*annakum mukhrajun*, "that you will be brought forth") is the *khabar* (predicate) of the first ﴿أنَّكُمْ﴾. The second ﴿أنَّكُمْ﴾ is a *ta'kid* (emphatic restatement) of it, used because the separation between the two was long.

﴿Far, far﴾ is an ism fi'l madi (a noun functioning as a past-tense verb) in the sense of a masdar (verbal noun), i.e., "it is far, far." ﴿for what you are promised﴾ refers to being brought out from the graves. The lam is extra, for clarification.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 37:

﴿In hiya﴾ i.e., what is life, ﴿illa hayatuna al-dunya namutu wa nahya﴾ ("There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live") by means of the lives of our children.
﴿He is none other than a man who has invented [a lie] against﴾ (what is meant by "he" is) the Messenger, ﴿and we do not believe in him﴾ as those who affirm the resurrection after death.

﴿He said: "In a little while"﴾, meaning: of time. And *ma* is *zāʾida* (an additional, redundant particle that does not change the meaning), ﴿they will surely become﴾, meaning: they will become, ﴿regretful﴾ over their disbelief and their denial.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 41:

﴿So the Cry seized them, justly﴾, the cry of punishment and destruction, ﴿and We made them into debris﴾, which is dried-up vegetation (ghuthaʾ), meaning We made them like it in dryness. ﴿So away with the wrongdoing people!﴾, away from mercy, ﴿the people who denied﴾.
﴿Then We brought into being after them other generations﴾ *(qurūnan)*: peoples.

﴿No community can precede its term﴾ by dying before it, ﴿nor can they delay it﴾ from it. The pronoun (الضمير, al-damir) was made masculine after the feminine noun (أمة, ummah) it refers to, out of regard for the meaning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 44:

﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession.﴾ Tatra (تَتْرى) is read with tanwin and without it, meaning consecutive, with a long period of time between each two. ﴿Every time there came to a nation its messenger, they denied him.﴾ The two hamzas are pronounced fully, and the second one is eased, between itself and the waw (ʾumma / ʾummatun is read with both hamzas, the second softened to a sound between hamza and waw). ﴿So We made them follow one another (in destruction).﴾ That is, in annihilation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 45:

﴿Then We sent Musa and his brother Harun with Our signs and a manifest authority﴾ (hujjah bayyinah), namely the hand and the staff, and other signs besides them.
To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they waxed proud (fastakbaroo) against belief in them and in God, and they were a haughty people (qawman ʿaliyin), dominating the Children of Israel by oppression.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 47:

﴿So they said, "Shall we believe in two humans like ourselves, while their people are servants to us?"﴾ obedient, submissive.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 49:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾ — the Torah — ﴿so that they [his people, the Children of Israel] might be guided﴾ by it away from misguidance. And it was given to him in its entirety after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 50:

﴿And We made the son of Maryam﴾ [i.e., ʿĪsā] ﴿and his mother a sign﴾. He did not say "two signs" because the sign in them both is one: his birth without a father (fahl).

﴿And We sheltered them both on a high ground﴾, a raised place, which was Bayt al-Maqdis, or Dimashq, or Filasṭīn, according to different opinions. ﴿Having a resting place﴾, i.e., level, on which its inhabitants settle. ﴿And a spring﴾, flowing water, apparent, seen by the eyes.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 51:

﴿O messengers, eat of the good things⌋ the lawful ones, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ of obligatory and voluntary kinds. ﴿Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do﴾, so I will reward you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 23, verse 52:

﴿And﴾ know that ﴿this﴾, that is, the religion of Islam, ﴿is your community﴾, your religion, O you who are addressed, that is, you must adhere to it, ﴿a single community﴾. This is a necessary circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl lāzima). In one canonical reading (qirāʼa) the nūn is lightened, and in another it is read with a kasra and shaddah, as a resumptive new sentence (istiʼnāf): ﴿And I am your Lord, so fear Me﴾, that is, beware of Me.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 53:

﴿So they broke their affair [i.e., the followers broke their religion] among themselves into sects﴾ [zuburan is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the subject of tafaqqa'u, meaning] groups differing from one another, like the Jews, the Christians and others, ﴿each party rejoicing in what they have﴾, i.e., in the religion they hold, ﴿rejoicing﴾, i.e., pleased with it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 54:

﴿So leave them﴾ (i.e., leave the disbelievers of Makkah) ﴿in their confusion﴾ (i.e., their misguidance) ﴿until a time﴾ (i.e., until the time of their death).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 55:

﴿Do they reckon that by what We extend to them﴾ — We give them — ﴿of wealth and children﴾ — in the worldly life.
﴿We hasten﴾ we expedite (nu‘ajjil) ﴿for them in good things﴾. No, rather ﴿they do not perceive﴾ that this is istidraj (a gradual leading toward ruin) for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 57:

﴿Indeed, those who are, out of fear of their Lord,﴾ their dread of Him ﴿apprehensive﴾ fearful of His punishment.
﴿And those who, in the signs of their Lord﴾ [i.e., the Qur'an] ﴿believe﴾ [i.e., affirm as true].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 59:

﴿And those who do not associate anything with their Lord﴾ with Him, anything else.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 60:

﴿And those who give﴾ yuʿṭūna (they give) ﴿what they give﴾ aʿṭaw (they gave) of the ṣadaqah (voluntary charity) and the righteous deeds (aʿmāl ṣāliḥah), ﴿and their hearts are fearful﴾ khāʾifah (fearing) that it will not be accepted from them. ﴿that they﴾ — the lām al-jarr (the preposition lām, "to" or "because") is understood before it.
*"And they are foremost in attaining it"* — in the knowledge of God.

ﷺ

"And We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity" (wus'aha), meaning its ability. So whoever is unable to pray standing, let him pray sitting; and whoever is unable to fast, let him feed (others) instead. "And with Us is a Book that speaks with the truth" (kitab yantiq bil-haqq), meaning: with Us, a record of what they did, namely the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), in which deeds are inscribed. "And they will not be wronged" (wa-hum la yuzlamun), meaning the acting souls will not be wronged in anything: no reduction will be made from the reward of good deeds, and no addition will be made to evil deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 63:

﴿Nay, their hearts are in ghamra﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, [immersed] in heedlessness (jahala) ﴿concerning this﴾ Qur'an, ﴿and they have deeds other than that﴾ which was mentioned for the believers, ﴿which they are doing﴾, so they will be punished for them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 23, verse 64:

﴿Hatta﴾ (until) is ibtida'iyya (introductory, marking the beginning of a new statement). ﴿When We seize their affluent ones﴾ their wealthy ones and their leaders ﴿with the punishment﴾ i.e., the sword, on the day of Badr. ﴿Behold, they cry out﴾ they wail loudly. It is said to them:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 65:

﴿Do not cry out today; indeed you will not be helped by Us.﴾ "Not protected" (lā tumna'ūn).
﴿Indeed, My verses were recited to you﴾ from the Qur'an, ﴿but you used to turn back on your heels, retreating﴾, i.e., going backwards (tarji'una al-qahqara).

Arabic terms: "مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ" (mustakbirin), "سامِرًا" (samiran), "تَهْجُرُونَ" (tahjurun).

﴿Arrogant﴾ regarding faith ﴿in it﴾, i.e., in the House or the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), because they are its people and are secure, unlike other people in their own lands. ﴿Talking nonsense﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning a group who converse at night around the House. ﴿Deserting﴾: from the triliteral form, you abandon the Qur'an; and from the quadriliteral form, i.e., you speak what is not the truth about the Prophet and the Qur'an.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 23, verse 68:

﴿Have they not then pondered over the Word?﴾ Its origin is yatadabbaruna (they ponder), and the taʾ was assimilated into the dal (idghām). ﴿The Word﴾ means the Qur'an, which indicates the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 70:

﴿Or do they say, "There is madness in him"?﴾ The interrogative (al-istifham) here is for affirmation (li-l-taqrir) of the truth: of the truthfulness of the Prophet, and the coming of messengers to the earlier nations, and their people's knowledge of his truthfulness and trustworthiness, and that there is no madness in him. ﴿Rather﴾ (bal) is for transition (li-l-intiqal), ﴿he has brought them the truth﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, which comprises the Oneness of God (al-tawhid) and the laws of Islam (shara'i' al-Islam).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 71:

﴿And if the Truth had followed their desires⦆ — i.e., the Qur'an — ﴿their desires﴾, by bringing what they desire of partners and offspring for Allah, exalted is Allah above that. ﴿The heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted﴾ — they would have departed from their observed order, because of the existence of mutual opposition in things, as is customary when there are multiple rulers. ﴿Rather, We have brought them their reminder﴾ — i.e., the Qur'an, in which is their reminder and their honour.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 72:

﴿Or do you ask them for any payment?﴾ (i.e., any wage) for what you have brought them of faith. ﴿But the payment of your Lord is better﴾ (i.e., His reward, His recompense, and His provision). In another reading, it is read as "kharjan" (kharj) in both places, and in another as "kharajan" (kharaj) in both. ﴿And He is the best of those who provide sustenance﴾ (i.e., the most excellent of those who give and reward).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 73:

﴿And indeed, you invite them to a path﴾ (ṣirāṭ), meaning a way, ﴿straight﴾, that is, the religion of Islam.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 74:

﴿And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ — [i.e., in] the resurrection, the reward and the punishment — ﴿are surely deviating from the path﴾ — i.e., the way — ﴿[away from it]﴾ — swerving from it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 75:

﴿Even if We had mercy upon them and removed the harm that is upon them﴾, i.e., the hunger that had afflicted them in Makkah for seven years, ﴿they would persist﴾, i.e., continue on, ﴿in their transgression﴾, i.e., their misguidance, ﴿wandering blindly﴾, i.e., hesitating and going back and forth.

"And We had already seized them with punishment," (the famine), "yet they did not humble themselves" (tawaduʿu) "to their Lord, nor did they supplicate" (yatadarraʿun), that is, "they did not turn eagerly to God in supplication."

"Until," (ḥattā) here is ibtidā'iyya (introducing a new statement), "when We open against them a gate of" — i.e., possessor of — "severe punishment," which is the Day of Badr, by slaughter; "in which they will be" — "despairing," utterly hopeless of every good.

﴿It is He who produced﴾ created ﴿for you hearing﴾ in the sense of the hearing faculties (al-asma'), ﴿and sight, and hearts﴾, meaning hearts, ﴿and hearts﴾ [af'idah], meaning hearts. ﴿Little is it that﴾ is an emphasis (ta'kid) on the smallness of the number.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 79:**

﴿And it is He who multiplied you upon the earth﴾ created you ﴿upon the earth, and to Him you will be gathered﴾ you will be resurrected.

﴿He it is who gives life﴾ by breathing the spirit into the lump of flesh, ﴿and causes death. And His is the alternation of night and day﴾ through blackness and whiteness, and through increase and decrease. ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ regarding His handiwork, exalted is He, ﴿so that you may take heed﴾.

﴿They said﴾, meaning the earlier ones: ﴿"When we have died and become dust, will we indeed be resurrected?"﴾ No.

Regarding the two hamzahs (الهمزتين) in the two places, there is tahqiq (التَّحْقِيق, pronouncing the hamzah fully) and tashil (تَسْهِيل الثَّانِيَة, softening the second hamzah), and inserting an alif (إدْخال أَلِف) between them, in both ways.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 83:

﴿We have indeed been promised this, we and our fathers, before﴾, i.e., the resurrection after death. ﴿Before﴾ [the Arabic is مِن قَبْل إنْ, where إنْ is] meaning ما (ma), "not": ﴿this is nothing but tales of the ancients﴾, lies of the ancients, like jokes and wonders. أَسَاطِير is the plural of أُسْطُورَة (usṭūrah), with a ḍammah on the first letter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 84:

﴿Say﴾ to them, ﴿"To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it" of creatures, ﴿if you know﴾ its Creator and its Owner?

﴿They will say, "To Allah."﴾ Say [to them]: ﴿"Will you not then remember?"﴾ with the second تَاء (tā') assimilated into الذَّال (dhāl) through idgham (assimilation of one consonant into the next), meaning: you would be admonished, and so you would know that the One who is able to create at the first instance is able to bring back to life after death.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 86:

﴿Say, "Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Great Throne?"﴾ [the Kursi (Footstool)]

Qur'an 23:87: "They will say, 'To Allah.' Say, 'Then will you not fear Him?'"

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: "Will you not be wary" (تَحْذَرُونَ) of worshipping other than Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 88:

﴿Say: "In whose hand is the dominion (malakut) of all things, and He protects while none can be protected against Him?"﴾ [malakut: mulk (dominion), and the ta' is for emphasis of intensity] ﴿and He protects (yujir) while none can be protected (yujar) against Him﴾ [yahmi (He protects/defends) and yuhma (is protected/defended) against Him]

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 89:

﴿They will say, "To Allah."﴾ And in another reading, "Li-Allah" with the lam of possession (lil-) in both places, taking into account that the meaning is "To whom belongs what has been mentioned?" ﴿Say, "Then how are you deluded?"﴾ You are deceived and turned away from the truth and from worshipping Allah alone; that is, how has it been imagined to you that it is false?

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 23, verse 90:**

﴿Rather, We have brought them the truth﴾ with sincerity, ﴿and indeed they are liars﴾ in their denial of it, and it is

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 91:

﴿Allah has not taken any son, and there has never been with Him any god. [If there were], then each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others.﴾ That is, if there were a god with Him, ﴿each god would have taken away what he created﴾: he would have been independent with it and would have prevented the other from seizing it, ﴿and some of them would have overcome others﴾ through contention, like the actions of the kings of this world. ﴿Exalted is Allah﴾ far above ﴿what they describe﴾ of the things mentioned.

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: what is hidden and what is seen. It is read in the genitive (jarr) as a sifah (qualifier, an adjective modifying "Allah"), and in the nominative (raf') as a khabar (predicate), with "He" (هُوَ) understood as an implied subject, meaning "He is the Knower..."

﴿Exalted is He﴾ (فَتَعالى): He is magnified, ﴿above what they associate﴾ (عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ) with Him, ـهُ, meaning "with Him" (مَعَهُ), as partners.

**Say: "My Lord, if You show me that which they are promised,"** Herein is idgham (assimilation, the merging of one sound into the next), in which the nun of in (إنْ), the conditional particle, is merged into ma (ما), the superfluous particle. **"that which they are promised"**: they are promised it, namely the punishment. **"it is true, namely the killing at Badr."**

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 94:**

﴿Rabbi, do not place me among the wrongdoing people.﴾ So (*fa-ahlik*) destroy me along with their destruction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 96:

﴿Repel evil with that which is better.﴾ That is, the quality of forgiveness and turning away from them, ﴿the evil﴾ being their harm to you. And this is before the command to fight. ﴿We know best what they describe﴾ — they lie and say [things], and We will recompense them for it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 97:**

﴿And say: "My Lord, I seek refuge"﴾ I take refuge ﴿in You from the promptings of the devils﴾, their incitements, ﴿with what they whisper﴾ to people.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 98:

﴿And I seek refuge with You, my Lord, from their presence﴾ in my affairs, for they only present themselves with evil.

"Until" (ḥattā) is inceptive (ibtidā'iyyah), introducing a new clause: ﴿until, when death comes to one of them﴾ and he sees his seat in the Fire and his seat in Paradise had he believed, ﴿he says, "My Lord, send me back"﴾. The plural form (ir-ji‘ūn, "send me back") is for glorification (al-ta‘ẓīm).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 100:

﴿That I may do righteousness﴾ by testifying that there is no deity except Allah, ﴿in that which I have left behind﴾, i.e., what I wasted of my life, meaning in exchange for it. ﴿No!﴾ i.e., there is no return. ﴿It is but a word he is saying﴾, i.e., "My Lord, send me back," and there is no benefit for him in it. ﴿And behind them is a barrier﴾, i.e., before them, a barrier that prevents them from returning ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾, and there is no return after it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 23, verse 101:

﴿Then when the Trumpet is blown﴾ (al-Sur): the horn, [blown for] the first blast or the second. ﴿there will be no kinship ties between them that day﴾ whereby they boast of them, ﴿nor will they ask about one another﴾ concerning them, contrary to their state in the world, because of what will preoccupy them of the magnitude of the matter, in some of the stations of the Resurrection; and in others they will regain consciousness. And in another verse: ﴿so they will turn to one another, questioning each other﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 102:

﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy﴾ with good deeds, ﴿those are the ones who will be successful﴾, the ones who will attain salvation.
﴿And whoever's scales are light﴾ [through evil deeds], ﴿those are the ones who have lost themselves﴾, ﴿they will abide forever in Hell﴾.
﴿The Fire scorches their faces﴾, burning them, ﴿and they therein are grimacing﴾, their upper and lower lips drawn back from their teeth, and it is said to them:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 105:

﴿Were not My verses﴾ of the Qur'an ﴿recited to you﴾, with which you were being warned?

﴿They will say, "Our Lord, our misery overcame us, and we were a people who went astray."﴾

In another recitation (qirāʾah), the word is read as شَقاوَتنا, with a fatḥah on its first letter and an alif after the first radical. Both forms, شِقْوَتنا and شَقاوَتنا, are verbal nouns (maṣdar), and they have the same meaning. "Who went astray" means they were astray from guidance.
﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return﴾ to opposition (al-mukhalafa).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 108:

﴿He said﴾ to them, through the tongue of Malik, after a period equal to the life of this world twice over, ﴿"Be silent therein"﴾, i.e., remain far away in the Fire, humiliated, ﴿"and do not speak to Me"﴾, concerning the lifting of the punishment from you, so that their hope may be cut off.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 23, verse 109:

﴿Indeed, there was a group of My servants﴾ They are the emigrants (al-muhajirun).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 23, verse 110:

﴿So you took them in derision﴾ — read with a ḍammah or a kasrah on the sīn (sukhriyyan, sikhriyyan), a verbal noun meaning mockery of them. [They were] Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Salman.

﴿until they made you forget My remembrance﴾ — so you abandoned it, because you were occupied with mocking them. Thus they were the cause of the forgetting, and it was attributed to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 111:

﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today﴾ with the everlasting bliss, ﴿for their patience﴾ under your mockery of them and your harm to them, ﴿that they, they are the triumphant﴾ in attaining what they sought. "Innahum" with a kasra on the hamza is a resumptive (isti'naf) sentence; with a fatha on it, it is the second object of "jazaytuhum" (I rewarded them).

﴿He said﴾: the Exalted said to them through the tongue of Malik. In another reading, the word is قُلْ (qul, "Say!"). ﴿How many years did you remain on the earth?﴾: in the world and in your graves. ﴿The number of years﴾: this is a tamyiz (a grammatical accusative that specifies the noun it follows).

﴿They said, "We stayed a day or part of a day."﴾ They were uncertain about that and considered it a short time, because of the magnitude of the punishment they were in. ﴿So ask those who count﴾, i.e., the angels (malā'ika) who keep account of the deeds of the creatures.

Allah says, through the tongue of Malik (the keeper of Hell), and in another reading "Qul" (say): ﴿Indeed, you remained not but a little, if only you had known.﴾ That is, the duration of your stay, in length, was little in comparison with your stay in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 115:

﴿Did you think that We created you in vain﴾ without any wisdom, ﴿and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ with the verb in the active voice (turjaʿūna, "you return") or the passive (turjaʿūna, "you are returned")? No indeed. Rather, We created you to worship Us through the command and the prohibition, and you will be returned to Us, and We will recompense you for that.

﴿Exalted is Allah﴾ above futility and anything else unbefitting Him, ﴿the King, the Truth. There is no god but Him, the Lord of the Noble Throne﴾. Al-Kursi (the seat, or footstool): it is the fine throne.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 23, verse 117:

﴿And whoever calls upon another god along with Allah, for which he has no proof﴾ – a descriptive qualifier (ṣifah kāshifah) with no implied restriction (mafhūm) [i.e., it does not imply that one who calls upon a god with proof would be excused]; ﴿then his reckoning is only with his Lord﴾ – i.e., his recompense; ﴿indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed﴾ – they will not attain happiness.

And say: "My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful."

Commentary: ﴿My Lord, forgive and have mercy﴾, [meaning, grant] the believers [more] in mercy than in forgiveness. ﴿And You are the best of the merciful﴾, the most excellent of those who show mercy.
